title: Buddy Bolden: his playing, his band and the Eagle Band
summary: Bocage recalls Bolden as a loud blues player, lists his sidemen, says Duson took over the band as the Eagle Band, and describes their keys and tempos.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Remember the drummer? Yeah. Put it off a minute. Peter Pocosch, 6th of February 1962, tape 3. I guess you're about one of the oldest playing musicians around, trumpet players. Can you remember any of the old time guys like Buddy Bolden and Whitman? Oh yeah.

I remember Buddy. I was quite young though. He died young too. He was an old fellow when he died. He must have been in his thirties, you know? What kind of trumpet playing did you make? Well he was mostly a blues player, you know? Mostly blues. He mostly make tunes, you know, like a pallet on the floor or blues and things like that. That's mostly the type of band they had, you know? Well he'd play jobs, you know? He'd play jobs, you know.

No, I mean would he play a job, you know? He'd play a job, you know? No, I mean would he play trumpet all the time when they were playing that number or would he let down and let the other instruments solo?

Oh yeah. All trumpet players are going to take down some, you know, but he can't stay up all the time. Oh yeah. All trumpet players are going to take down some, you know, but he can't stay up all the time. Do you remember who was in Buddy's band when you saw him? the bass palette on the floor, the blues and things like that. That's mostly the type band they had, you know.
Would he play all the time? Well he'd play a job, you know. No, I mean would he play trumpet all the time when they were playing that number, or would he let down and let the other instruments solo?
Oh yeah, all trumpet players are going to take down some units, he can't step all the time.
Do you remember who was in Buddy's band when you saw him?

I might remember a few of those fellas. I think he was Buddy, and the Runs of Stores, Bob Lyons, Cornish was playing trombone. I think Brock Mumford was playing, yes, Brock Mumford was playing guitar, and a fella called Frank Lewis was a clarinet player. And I think Jamesy Phillips up here played the drums. You see when Bowling went crazy, you know, he's the Hart and Jackson. Well Frankie Dewson took the band then. The same fellas that Bowling had, Frankie took them over and called it the Eagle Band, see. He was a trombone player, see. Well instead of Bowling, he had a fella called Edward Clem, an old trumpet player. He was a figure too, you know, head man. Well then I played violin with them, with Eagle Band, see. What kind of prizes did you see Buddy playing then? Well playing these balls, you know. Playing the ball. He didn't play nothing but dances once in a while, like the old Masonic Hall, or maybe we used to have lawn parties those days, you know, open air dances, you know. And that's mostly what they would play, you know.
Was he a loud trumpet player? Yeah, oh yeah, he was loud.
That was his biggest asset, you know. That was his biggest asset he had was blowing, you know, he could blow.
Did he have a big tongue?
Yeah, he was pretty good. He had a pretty fat tongue and everything, yeah. But the only thing, he didn't know what he was doing, you know, he just picked it up, you know.
Did Buddy know what key he was playing?

Well I don't know, because you see those fellas they mostly play, you know, maybe B flat, or maybe E flat, or maybe one sharp, and that's the limit, you see. But when you get around three or four flats or three or four sharps, well then they're out, you see, you see. So you just can see, well, most everything they played was in B flat or F or something like that, you know.
Did they play a lot of blues down there?
Yeah, oh yeah, that was it. Stand by them blues and everything. Slow blues? Tied on the flow blues and… Did they play them very slow? Yeah, they used to call it slow drag those days, you know.
Did they play many fast numbers?
No, not those, they didn't play nothing too fast, just a medium tempo, you know.
